newsitem.title: CHINA: HK people return Deng stamps because of wrinkle.
newsitem.headline: HK people return Deng stamps because of wrinkle.

text.p: Hong Kong people usually queue in their thousands to buy new-issue postage stamps, but on Monday they lined up at post offices to hand back stamps bearing the face of late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping.
The Deng stamp, the first mainland Chinese issue to go on sale in Hong Kong, had been snapped up over the weekend by hundreds of collectors and dealers.

Once buyers got them home, though, some found them too wrinkled and grainy. Three out of five of the stamps, a series marking Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1, had been badly printed, they complained.
Queues built up again on Monday to return the stamps.
Some buyers were quoted as saying the quality was poor because the stamps were Chinese-made. A spokesman said the Hong Kong Post Office would return the flawed stamps to China.
The Chinese leader, who died last February, was widely credited with devising the "one country, two systems" policy which was used to reunify Hong Kong with China.

New stamp issues here often whip up a buying frenzy, soaring 10 times in value within days. Demand is further stoked by collectors and dealers from the mainland, a market of 1.2 billion potential philatelists.
